Privacy policy Effective November 19, 2026 Covers commutescout.com, the MCP server and API, and the CommuteScout Drive apps. CommuteScout is an independent project run by one person in California (“we”, “us”). This policy says what we collect, why, who helps us process it, how long we keep it, and how you can see or delete it. The code behind the service is open source, so you can check any of this yourself. The short version A summary for convenience. The numbered sections below are the policy. No account needed for the map, routes, the assistant, the MCP server or the API. Without one we keep no profile of you. No ads, no tracking cookies, no cross-site tracking. We do not sell your personal information or share it for advertising. With an account we store your email address and what you save: watch areas, places, plugin choices, settings and API keys. Location is used to answer what you ask: a route, the area on screen, alerts ahead. Our own logs round coordinates to about a kilometer. Road reports are public. Others see what you reported and where, never your name or email. You can delete your account yourself in the app or on the web, or ask us at privacy@commutescout.com . We are responsible for the personal information described here. It does not cover plugins run by other people, the AI assistant you connect our MCP server to, app stores, or the agencies whose public data we show. Each of those has its own terms and privacy policy. 02 What we collect and why # Using the site, map and assistant without an account The area you are looking at. To draw conditions, the map asks our server for the area on screen or the route you planned. Route and address searches are sent to our server to answer them. Your approximate area, once. The map opens on your region without asking for location permission: our CDN, Cloudflare, estimates a city-level position from your IP address, we round it to about a kilometer, and we use it only to choose the first view. We do not store or log it. Without that estimate, your browser’s time zone, read on your device, picks a region instead. Precise location, only if you ask. If you choose “Use my location” in the route planner, your browser asks your permission and then gives the map your position, which is sent to our server as the start of the route. Assistant questions. What you type is sent to Anthropic to generate the answer and is logged by us to improve answers. The log entry carries a visitor code made from a salted hash of your IP address that changes every day, never the address itself. If you rate an answer with “Was this right?”, the vote is logged with the question the same way. Page events. The map records a few interaction events, such as a page view, with the same daily-changing visitor code and nothing else. Accounts An account is optional. It is needed for watch areas, road reports, syncing places and plugins, and API keys. When you sign in with Google, with Apple (in the iPhone app) or with an email link, we receive your email address and a user ID from that sign-in. Accounts are managed with Google Firebase Authentication and stored in Google Cloud Firestore. Sign-in emails are sent through Resend. Watch areas and alerts Watch areas are an invite-only trial. For each area we store its name, its shape (a circle, a drawn outline or a route), the kinds of events you want, your alert settings (push or email, quiet hours with your time zone, and whether to hear when something clears), and a record of alerts already sent so you are not told twice. To deliver alerts we store, per device, the browser push subscription or the app’s push token, and we send email alerts to your account address through Resend. Your browser or phone asks your permission before notifications are turned on. Places, plugin choices and settings When you are signed in, the places you save or go to (Home, Work, up to 20 favorites and up to 20 recent destinations, each with a name and coordinates) sync to your account so they follow you between devices. We also store the plugins you switched off, any private plugin you added by address together with the access token you gave it, and settings such as units. Road reports and votes When you post a report (what you saw, where, which way you were heading, and any note you add), we store it with your account ID so daily limits and voting work. It is shown to everyone on the map and in our public data files until it expires, which takes between 20 minutes and a day depending on the kind, without your name, email or account ID. Your votes on reports (“still there” or “gone”) are stored with the report the same way. See who receives data for how reports reach plugins. Shared trips If you share a trip, we store the start and end names, the route, its distance, time and directions so the link works. Anyone with the link can open it. It is not tied to your account. API keys, the MCP server and the REST API For each API key we store its name, a one-way hash of its secret (never the secret itself), your account ID and email, when it was created and last used, and your account’s request count for the day. Each request made with a key is logged with the key ID, the path and the result. Each MCP tool call is logged with the tool name, whether it worked and how long it took, never its arguments. The places and coordinates in a request are used to answer it, which can mean passing them to the routing, address, traffic and weather providers listed below. Requests made with your key can read your saved places, so treat a key like a password. Your IP address is used in memory to apply the limits on requests made without a key. The CommuteScout Drive apps Location. With your permission, the apps use your device’s precise location to guide you and to warn you about what is ahead. While you are navigating, they keep using it with the screen off or the app in the background (on Android, with an ongoing notification), so spoken directions and alerts keep working. They do not use location in the background when you are not navigating. What reaches our server. The apps send us your position and the next stretch of your route to fetch conditions and alerts ahead, your start and destination to plan routes, your position and heading to look up the speed limit, the route when you save an offline map for a trip, and your approximate position (about 100 meters) with an assistant question. We use these to answer the request. For plugin alerts, positions are rounded to a grid of about 5 to 10 kilometers before they are kept in memory or sent to a plugin. On your phone only. Downloaded maps and voices, the trip in progress, unsent reports and the iPhone app’s drive log stay on the phone. Spoken directions are generated on the phone. The drive log leaves it only if you share it yourself from Settings. No analytics or ad code. The apps contain no analytics, crash-reporting or advertising SDKs and do not read your device’s advertising identifier. They use Firebase for sign-in and push notifications; Firebase Cloud Messaging creates an installation ID to deliver them. When you write to us The contact form sends us the name, email address and message you type, as an email delivered through Resend; a Cloudflare Turnstile check confirms you are a person. If you joined the Pro waitlist, we store that email address only to tell you when Pro launches. We do not add you to any other list. Analytics and logs Visit counts. The website uses Cloudflare Web Analytics, which counts page views and load times without cookies or device identifiers and does not follow you across sites. Our application logs round coordinates to about a kilometer and identify visitors only by the daily-changing code above. A request that fails with a server error may be logged in more detail so we can fix it. Request logs. Our hosting provider (Google Cloud) and our CDN (Cloudflare) keep standard request logs: the time, the address requested (which can include map coordinates), the response, the browser or app version, and the network address the request came from. We use them only to run, secure and debug the service. We do not build profiles of you or draw inferences about you from any of this. 03 Cookies, local storage and Do Not Track # The public site sets no cookies of its own and uses no advertising or cross-site tracking technology. Your browser keeps a few settings in local storage on your device: the base map, units, the panel you had open, the plugins you switched on or off, and the email address you typed to sign in by link. For the current tab only, it also remembers where the map was looking. Signing in keeps your session in your browser’s storage through Firebase. Google’s sign-in window and the Turnstile check on the contact form are run by Google and Cloudflare under their own policies. Do Not Track. We do not change our behavior in response to Do Not Track signals, because there is nothing to switch off: we do not track you across other sites, and we do not allow other companies to do so through our service. 04 Who receives data # These service providers process data for us to run the service, under their own terms, and each receives only what its job needs. We do not sell or rent personal information to anyone. Service providers and other recipients Recipient What for What they see Google Cloud and Firebase Hosting, database, sign-in, push to the apps (Firebase Cloud Messaging), request logs What the service stores, as our host Cloudflare CDN and security in front of the site, visit counts, map and data files, the contact form check Your IP address and the requests you make, as any CDN does Anthropic Generating assistant answers Your question, earlier questions in the same chat, and the app's approximate location if sent Resend Sign-in emails, alert emails, contact form messages Email addresses and message content Stadia Maps Routing, address search, speed limits, matching a point to a road Coordinates and place names in the request, sent by our server TomTom Live traffic speeds Road coordinates being checked, sent by our server National Weather Service Forecasts and weather alerts Coordinates our server asks about OpenFreeMap Map tiles for two of the base map styles Your IP address and the map area you view, from your browser or app Apple, Google, Mozilla, Microsoft Delivering push notifications to phones and browsers The notification and your device's push token GitHub Hosting the apps' voice downloads Your IP address when you download a voice Plugin operators Plugins add alerts from sources other than public agencies, and some are run by other people. Our server asks plugins about areas rounded to about 5 to 10 kilometers, under our own identity, never yours. When you post a report, it is also sent to the public plugins you have switched on that accept that kind of report, under a separate pseudonym for each plugin instead of your account or email; your votes on a plugin’s alerts go to that plugin the same way. A plugin you add by address in the app is contacted by your phone directly, so it sees your IP address, the approximate center of your map and the access token you gave it. Only plugins run by CommuteScout itself ever receive your sign-in token. Your AI assistant If you connect our MCP server to an AI assistant, what our tools return, including your saved places when you use an API key, goes to that assistant and its provider under their privacy policy. Public agencies and camera images Our server fetches public feeds from state and federal agencies (listed on Data sources ); they receive nothing about you. Some camera images load in your browser or app directly from the agency’s image host, which sees that request the way any image load does. Legal reasons We may disclose information if the law requires it, to protect someone’s safety, or to protect the service and its users from fraud or abuse. If the project were ever transferred to someone else, this policy would keep applying to the data transferred with it. 05 No sale, no sharing for advertising # We do not sell personal information and do not “share” it for cross-context behavioral advertising, as California law defines those terms, and have not done so in the past 12 months. We show no ads. We do not use personal information to make automated decisions about you. The only sensitive personal information we collect is the location described above, and we use it only to provide what you ask for. 06 How long we keep it # Retention periods Data Kept for Account, watch areas, places, plugin choices, settings, API keys Until you delete them or your account Push subscriptions and app push tokens Until you sign out of the app on that device, delete the account, or the push service reports the device gone Road reports and their votes Shown for 20 minutes to a day depending on the kind; set to be deleted from storage two days after posting Shared trips 180 days, then deleted automatically Application and request logs, including assistant questions About 30 days, the standard log retention of our hosting provider Contact form messages In our email until the conversation is finished Pro waitlist email Until Pro launches or you ask us to remove it Approximate map location from your IP address Not stored Separately, we keep a long-term archive of public road events (incidents, closures, chain controls and fires as the agencies publish them) for history features. It contains no data about users. 07 Your choices and rights # See and change your data. Signed in, you can view and edit your watch areas, places, plugins, alert settings and API keys in the app or in the map’s Settings and Watch panels. Notifications. Turn them off per device in your phone or browser settings, or switch push and email alerts off in your alert settings. Location. You can deny or revoke location permission at any time in your browser or phone settings. The map still works; the apps cannot guide you without it. Ask us. Wherever you live, you can ask us what personal information we hold about you and what we do with it, for a copy, to correct it, or to delete it. Email privacy@commutescout.com from the address on your account. We may ask you to confirm the request from that address before we act on it, and we answer within 45 days. Someone you authorize can ask for you if they show us your signed permission. No penalty. We will not deny you the service, charge you differently or give you a worse service because you used any of these rights. California residents: the rights above include the rights to know, delete, correct and limit the use of sensitive personal information under the California Consumer Privacy Act, as amended by the CPRA. We do not sell or share personal information, so there is nothing to opt out of; we treat a Global Privacy Control signal as an opt-out request all the same. Under California’s “Shine the Light” law: we do not disclose personal information to third parties for their direct marketing. 08 Deleting your account # In the app: Settings, then your account, then Delete account. On the web: sign in on the map , open Settings and choose Delete my account (the same button is on the watch page ). By email: write to privacy@commutescout.com from the address on your account. Deleting immediately removes your account record (with your saved places, plugin choices and settings), all watch areas and their alert history, every registered device, and all API keys with their usage counts, so a key stops working at once. Deleting in the app also removes your sign-in record. Deleting on the web leaves your sign-in record (your email address and sign-in method) in Firebase Authentication; to remove it as well, delete from the app or email us and we will. Reports you posted never showed your identity and expire on their own, as described above. Copies in logs age out on the schedule above. 09 California disclosures # The categories of personal information we have collected in the past 12 months, where they come from, why we use them and who receives them. Details are in what we collect and who receives data . California categories of personal information Category Examples Source Purpose Disclosed to Identifiers Email address, account ID, API key ID, push tokens, IP address You; your browser or phone; Google or Apple sign-in Accounts, alerts, limits, security Google Cloud and Firebase, Resend, Cloudflare, push services Precise geolocation (sensitive) Device position in the apps or with Use my location; saved places; watch areas You; your browser or phone Routes, alerts ahead, nearby conditions, answering questions Google Cloud, Stadia Maps, Anthropic (approximate only), plugin operators (rounded to 5 to 10 km) Internet activity Requests, pages viewed, tool calls, errors Your browser, app or API client Running, securing and improving the service Google Cloud, Cloudflare Content you provide Assistant questions, road reports, contact messages You Answering you, showing reports to others Anthropic, Resend, plugin operators (reports, under a pseudonym), the public (reports) 10 Visitors outside the United States # CommuteScout is built for US roads and run from the United States. Our servers run in Google Cloud’s us-west1 region, and the providers above process data in the US. If you use the service from elsewhere, your information is transferred to and processed in the US. If laws such as the EU or UK GDPR apply to you, we rely on these legal bases: providing the service you asked for (accounts, alerts, places, reports); our legitimate interest in running, securing and improving the service (logs, limits, visit counts); and your consent where we ask for it (location and notification permissions, which you can withdraw in your device settings). You can use the rights in your choices and rights , object to processing based on legitimate interest, and complain to your local data protection authority. 11 Children # CommuteScout is not directed to children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from them. You must be at least 13 to create an account. If you believe a child under 13 has given us personal information, email privacy@commutescout.com and we will delete it. 12 Security # Connections are encrypted with HTTPS. API key secrets are stored only as one-way hashes, the apps keep plugin tokens in the phone’s secure storage, and access to stored data is limited to the operator. No system is perfectly secure. If a breach affects your personal information, we will tell you as the law requires. To report a security problem, see our security policy . 13 Changes to this policy # We will post any change here with a new effective date. If a change is material, we will also email account holders before it takes effect. We will not use personal information we already hold in a materially different way without your consent. 14 Contact # Privacy requests: privacy@commutescout.com . Anything else: hello@commutescout.com . The code is open source at github.com/nicglazkov/commutescout . See also the terms of use .
